title: A weighted vote and its tie
question: Three aligned class-1 probabilities are .8,.4,.3 with relative member weights 1,1,2. Calculate hard-vote share, mean probability and decisions. Then change A to .9.
hint: Normalize by total 4. An exact final tie chooses class 0.
solution: Only A votes 1, so the weighted hard share is 1/4 and the hard decision 0. The soft mean is (.8+.4+2×.3)/4=.45, also class 0. Changing A to .9 gives .475 without changing the hard ballot. A soft tie would require A=1: (1+.4+.6)/4=.5, still class 0 under the declared tie. The observed target has not been supplied, so none of these decisions establishes correctness.

title: Fit a changed cancellation weight
question: A has residuals [−2,2] hours and B[1,1] on two permitted combination rows. Find the best convex A weight and combined MSE. Would adding B help an A with residuals [0,0]?
solution: Their mean square is [(1−3w)²+(1+w)²]/2=1−2w+5w². Derivative−2+10w vanishes at w=.2, inside [0,1]. Residuals are [.4,1.2], MSE .8 hours²; member MSEs are 4 and 1. If A is exact, w=1 gives zero. Forcing an equal mean with B creates .25 hours² loss. The identity bounds the weighted member average, not the best member; fitted weights still need untouched assessment.

title: Separate correlation and copying
question: At a fixed query, four random fitted forecasts each have variance 9 and every pair correlation 1/3. Find average variance. Could their common correlation instead be−.5?

title: A smaller bag and missing votes

title: Update different weak errors
question: Compute signed AdaBoost α for ε=.3 and .45. After each optimal normalized update, what mass lies on this stump's wrong rows? What happens at .5 and 0?

It is half the distribution's mass, not half the rows or the accumulated ensemble's error. At .5 the coefficient is zero, with no positive edge. title: A bound with shrinking edges
question: Accepted rounds have γ_t=1/[4(t+1)] for t≥1. Does the derived bound guarantee uniform exponential decrease to zero?
solution: Every edge is positive but no positive constant lower-bounds them all. Σγ_t²=(1/16)Σ_{t≥1}1/(t+1)² is finite, so exp(−2Σγ_t²) tends to a positive value. This upper bound therefore does not establish convergence to zero. That absence of a guarantee is not proof that actual training error fails to improve.

title: Time and entity ownership
question: A machine contributes hourly rows; the task is a previously unseen machine next month. A shuffled row split holds some hours from every machine, and a globally fitted scaler precedes stacking. Identify the problems and propose an assessment boundary.
hint: Separate entity, time and preprocessing permissions.
solution: Sibling machine information crosses fit/test, later times can influence earlier fits, and the scaler learns from evaluation features. Reserve later observations from machines absent from training as the outer test. Inside outer training, generate meta predictions respecting the corresponding entity/time/label-availability restrictions and fit preprocessing only within each permitted fit. Early rows without legal predictions remain masked out of meta fitting. The exact policy must match how new machines arrive; GroupKFold alone does not enforce chronology.

title: Calibration is not preserved by an average
question: In the fair-signal law, condition on mean forecast .75 and .5. What are the event rates? Why can the mean nevertheless have lower Brier risk?
hint: List signal pairs producing the same forecast.
solution: Mean .75 occurs only when both high signals occur, with true rate 1. Mean .5 occurs in the two cross-signal states, each with true rate .5. The .75 group is uncalibrated. The pointwise squared-loss identity still reduces loss relative to average member loss, and averaging over the exact law gives mean risk 5/32 versus member 3/16. Calibration and this proper-risk comparison answer different questions.

title: Account for training and serving
question: Four bases, five folds and 1000 rows: count base fits, rows per fold fit and row processing under linear fit cost. Member serving times are 3,8,2,5 ms, meta 1 ms. Give ideal sequential and parallel totals.
hint: Include fold fits and final full-data refits.
solution: 20 fold fits plus 4 full-data fits; each fold fit receives 800 rows. Row work is 20×800+4×1000=20000, plus meta fitting. Sequential serving totals 3+8+2+5+1=19 ms; ideal parallel branches plus meta max(3,8,2,5)+1=9 ms. The served collection has 4 bases and 1 meta learner, not 20 fold models. Actual overhead, batching, contention and tail latency require separate measurement.

title: Align named classes

solution: The aligned vector is [.6,.3,.1]. Amber receives its .6 even though its new column is first. Adding [.1,.6,.3] by position would call silver mass amber, amber mass blue and blue mass silver. title: Project a changed coefficient vector
question: Project [.8,.3,−.1] onto the simplex. Compare with clip-and-normalize and explain why they differ.
hint: Test the active first two sorted coordinates and their common threshold.
solution: Their threshold is (.8+.3−1)/2=.05. Subtract it from the two active values and floor the third at zero, giving [.75,.25,0]. Clipping first gives [.8,.3,0], then dividing by 1.1 gives [8/11,3/11,0]. Both are permitted simplex points, but only the common-threshold point is the Euclidean closest vector. The distinct distances and derivative/KKT conditions identify the actual projection, not mere feasibility.

title: Find indirect selection leakage
question: A base predicts held rows A/D after fitting its coefficients only on B,C,E,F. Its regularization setting was chosen using targets from all A–F. Is its OOF cell honest? Repair the procedure.
hint: Trace selection-label access as well as coefficient-fit access.
solution: It is not honest: A and D influenced the selected setting used by their supposed held prediction. Perform setting selection within the permitted B,C,E,F subset, fit the selected rule there, then predict A/D. Repeat that complete choice-and-fit workflow for every OOF fold. If assessing the whole stack, surround all of it with an outer boundary whose labels teach none of those decisions. The nested program logs both kinds of access; a clean coefficient-fit list alone misses this fault.

title: Repair stale serving state
question: A saved bundle's first two feature names are swapped, but scaler arrays, base parameters, meta weights and old metrics are retained. Can updating only its checksum make it a valid new measured rule?
hint: A checksum binds bytes; ask whether those bytes still mean the fitted columns.
solution: No. The arrays now read different inputs than their fitted schema specifies. Restore the correct feature order or transform every affected parameter/preprocessing mapping consistently as a declared equivalent state, with a forward correspondence check. If the transformation changes the rule rather than preserving it, fit/version/evaluate that changed workflow under a new boundary. A recomputed checksum does not establish semantic correspondence or allow borrowing old test metrics. The live saved-state view rejects the stale feature mapping and preserves explicit invalid-state feedback.
